group: No discriminator – exactly one schema validates (happy path)

input.value: JSON node that satisfies schema[0] and fails schema[1]

cases.expected: empty ValidationMessage set (no errors) – numberOfValidSchema == 1, errors stays null
cases.description: When discriminator is disabled and exactly one of the supplied schemas validates, OneOfValidator must return an empty error set.

group: No discriminator – no schema validates

input.value: JSON node that fails all schemas

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message with key "oneOf" and argument "0" (no valid schemas)
cases.description: When none of the schemas validate, OneOfValidator must produce a oneOf error with numberOfValidSchema == 0.

group: No discriminator – multiple schemas validate, short‑circuit allowed

input.value: JSON node that satisfies schema[0] and schema[1]

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message with key "oneOf.indexes", arguments "2" and "0, 1" (two valid schemas). Child errors may be present if schemas produce them, but the main message must be oneOf.indexes.
cases.description: When more than one schema validates and canShortCircuit() returns true, the loop breaks after the second match; the validator must still report a oneOf.indexes error because numberOfValidSchema != 1.

group: No discriminator – multiple schemas validate, short‑circuit NOT allowed

input.value: JSON node that satisfies three schemas

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message with key "oneOf.indexes", arguments "3" and "0, 1, 2" (three valid schemas). Loop iterates over all schemas because canShortCircuit() returns false.
cases.description: Ensures the validator does not break early when short‑circuiting is disabled and still reports a oneOf.indexes error.

group: Discriminator enabled – matching discriminator found

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=true, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node with property "type":"A" (discriminator property present)

cases.expected: empty ValidationMessage set if the schema referenced by "$ref" matches the discriminator value; otherwise a oneOf error as in the non‑discriminator case.
cases.description: When discriminator is enabled and the node contains the discriminator property that maps to a $ref of the currently evaluated schema, the validator marks a match, collects child errors only from the matching schema and ultimately returns no error if that schema validates.

group: Discriminator enabled – discriminator property missing (ignore path)

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=false, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node without the discriminator property

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a oneOf error (same rules as without discriminator) because the context is marked as ignore and childErrors are aggregated from all schemas.
cases.description: If the discriminator property is absent, the context is marked ignore; the validator must fall back to normal handling and report a oneOf error when the number of valid schemas is not exactly one.

group: Discriminator enabled – no matching schema and not ignored

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=true, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node with discriminator property "type":"UNKNOWN" that does not match any $ref

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message built from message().instanceNode(...).arguments("based on the provided discriminator. No alternative could be chosen based on the discriminator property")
cases.description: When discriminator is enabled, a discriminator validator exists, but none of the schemas match the discriminator value, the validator must produce the special error indicating that no alternative could be chosen.

group: Discriminator enabled – mapping overrides discriminator value

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=false, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node with discriminator property "type":"A" (mapping contains "A" -> "B")

cases.expected: empty ValidationMessage set because the discriminator mapping changes the value from "A" to "B" and the schema being evaluated has a $ref of "B", thus a match is recorded and the matched schema validates.
cases.description: When a discriminator is enabled and the discriminator property value is remapped via the discriminator's mapping, the validator must use the mapped value to compare against the schema's $ref. If they match and the schema validates, the result should be success (no errors).

group: Discriminator enabled – discriminator present but schema lacks $ref

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=true, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message with key "oneOf" and argument "0" (no valid schemas). The lack of $ref means the discriminator cannot mark a match, so normal one‑of logic applies.
cases.description: If the discriminator property is present but the candidate schema does not contain a $ref, the discriminator matching logic cannot succeed. The validator should fall back to the regular oneOf evaluation and report an error when no schema validates.

group: Discriminator enabled – matching discriminator but schema validation fails

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=false, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node with discriminator property "type":"A" that maps to a schema whose internal validation fails

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message with key "oneOf" and argument "0" plus the child errors produced by the failing schema. Because a discriminator match was found but the matched schema is invalid, the validator must report the normal oneOf error together with the child errors.
cases.description: When a discriminator match is identified but the matched schema itself produces validation errors, the validator should not return the special "no alternative could be chosen" message. Instead it should behave like a normal oneOf failure, reporting the oneOf error and the child errors from the matched schema.

group: Discriminator enabled – exactly one schema validates (happy path with discriminator)

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=true, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node with discriminator property "type":"B" that matches the $ref of schema[1] and satisfies that schema

cases.expected: empty ValidationMessage set (no errors) – numberOfValidSchema == 1, errors stays null, childErrors contain only errors from the matched schema (which are none).
cases.description: The typical successful path when discriminators are enabled: the node contains the discriminator property, it maps to a $ref that points to exactly one schema, and that schema validates. The validator should return an empty set.

group: Discriminator enabled – multiple schemas validate (oneOf.indexes error despite match)

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=false, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active, canShortCircuit=false)
JSON node with discriminator property "type":"C" that matches schema[0] $ref, but the node also satisfies schema[1] and schema[2]

cases.expected: ValidationMessage set containing a single message with key "oneOf.indexes", arguments "3" and "0, 1, 2" (three valid schemas). The presence of a discriminator match does not suppress the oneOf.indexes error because more than one schema validates.
cases.description: Even when a discriminator match is found, the oneOf rule still requires exactly one matching schema. If several schemas validate, the validator must report a oneOf.indexes error listing all matching indexes.

group: ExecutionContext failFast flag restoration

input.value: JSON node that fails all schemas

cases.expected: After validate() returns, executionContext.isFailFast() == true (original value restored). The method returns a ValidationMessage set with key "oneOf" and argument "0".
cases.description: The validator temporarily sets failFast to false while iterating over child schemas. This test verifies that the original failFast flag is restored in the finally block, regardless of validation outcome.

group: Walk flag true with discriminator enabled – matching discriminator

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (failFast=false, discriminator enabled, DiscriminatorContext active)
JSON node with discriminator property "type":"D" that matches $ref of schema[0] and the schema validates only when walk() is used

cases.expected: empty ValidationMessage set – the validator called schema.walk() for each child schema, the discriminator matched, and the matched schema produced no errors.
cases.description: Ensures that when walk == true the validator invokes the walk() method on child schemas, and that discriminator handling works identically for the walk path.

group: Null ExecutionContext – NPE on isFailFast

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When executionContext is null the first call to executionContext.isFailFast() throws NPE.

group: Null node with discriminator enabled – NPE on node.get

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When discriminator is enabled the validator accesses node.get(propertyName). If node is null a NPE is thrown.

group: Null validationContext in OneOfValidator – NPE on getConfig

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If the OneOfValidator instance has its validationContext field set to null, the call this.validationContext.getConfig() throws NPE.

group: Parent schema missing – NPE on getValidators

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When getParentSchema() returns null, the subsequent call .getValidators() results in NPE while trying to locate a discriminator validator.

group: Discriminator validator type mismatch – ClassCastException

cases.expected: ClassCastException
cases.description: If a validator with keyword "discriminator" is present but is not an instance of DiscriminatorValidator, the cast ((DiscriminatorValidator) …) throws ClassCastException.

group: Discriminator property name null – NPE on isEmpty

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When discriminator.getPropertyName() returns null, the subsequent call .isEmpty() throws NPE.

group: Discriminator mapping null – NPE on getOrDefault

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If discriminator.getMapping() returns null, the call .getOrDefault(...) throws NPE while trying to resolve the mapped value.

group: Schema node null – NPE on get("$ref")

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If a child schema's getSchemaNode() returns null, the later call .get("$ref") on a null object throws NPE.

group: enterDiscriminatorContext throws RuntimeException – propagation

input.value: mock ExecutionContext where enterDiscriminatorContext throws IllegalStateException

cases.expected: IllegalStateException
cases.description: When discriminator is enabled the validator calls executionContext.enterDiscriminatorContext. If that method throws, the exception propagates out of validate().

group: canShortCircuit overridden to throw – exception propagation

input.value: JSON node that validates at least two schemas

cases.expected: RuntimeException
cases.description: A subclass of OneOfValidator overrides canShortCircuit() to throw RuntimeException. The validate() method does not catch it, so the exception bubbles up.

group: reportChildErrors throws – exception propagation

input.value: mock ExecutionContext (discriminator disabled) where reportChildErrors throws IllegalArgumentException
JSON node that fails all schemas

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: When discriminator is disabled and a schema produces errors, validate() calls reportChildErrors(executionContext). If that method throws, the exception propagates.
